prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form that made incretin-based therapies for diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: All six of us placed B034 first, which tells us little about merit by itself, so I rest the case on the science. The chain from proglucagon processing, through identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) amide and its insulinotropic and incretin actions, to receptor biology and long-acting agonists is unusually clear and original. It has been confirmed by several independent large outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal disease, so maturity is not in doubt and the work is arguably overdue. It fits the physiology-to-medicine tradition of the prize. A three-person prize built on the basic discoverers (Holst for the physiology of the incretin effect and active forms, Drucker for receptor biology and translational concept, Mojsov for identification and synthesis of the active peptide) keeps the citation about discovery and avoids a dispute over which company's drug deserves credit.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the real weakness. Habener's group and Mojsov's priority for the active form are contested in the literature, Knudsen's medicinal chemistry is what actually produced the drugs most patients take, and a three-name limit forces an arbitrary cut. If the committee concluded that the discovery of the active peptide cannot be assigned cleanly, a prize centred on B034 would be fragile, and B003 (unfolded protein response, a tidy Walter and Mori pair with only a partial disease-translation record) would be the safer alternative. A prize that favours basic discoverers over the industrial developers may also be seen as incomplete for a therapy defined by its pharmacology.

responses.point: Svenningsson ranks B034 first but proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, treating Mojsov's credit as contested and not resolvable from the supplied text, and he ranks cGAS-STING (B029) third.
responses.response: I take the Mojsov problem seriously, but I would not drop her because the credit is contested. The disagreement is about priority and shared work with Habener, and a prize for discovery should follow the identification of the active peptide, not the later drug. Putting Knudsen in the trio shifts the citation toward industrial drug design and away from physiology, which I think is a worse description of what the committee is rewarding. On B029, I agree that cGAS-STING is mechanistically clean and relevant to autoimmunity and interferonopathies, from my own field. The therapeutic payoff is still in trials, so I would not rank it above B003 or B040 this year.

responses.point: Linnarsson places BCR-ABL inhibition and imatinib (B027) second, as the template of molecularly targeted cancer therapy, and ranks the unfolded protein response (B003) only sixth.
responses.response: I agree that imatinib is exceptionally clear and mature. My reservation is attribution. The BCR-ABL fusion discovery and the oncogene biology (Rowley, Nowell, Groffen and others) sit outside the credited names, and a prize to Druker, Sawyers and Lydon alone would reward the drug program over the origin of the target. For B003 I disagree with the low rank. Walter and Mori are a clean, complementary pair, and the mechanism has been replicated over three decades in yeast, mammals and many disease settings, so I rank it above B027 as the second candidate.

responses.point: Sandberg ranks B034 first as an unusually clear arc from hormone physiology to medicine and B003 second, and he also sees B040 (CAR-T) as clinically substantial but not yet complete for cancer in general.
responses.response: I share his order for the top two and his caution on CAR-T. I would add that CAR-T's attribution is difficult: Eshhar's early chimeric receptor concept is outside the credited names, and Rosenberg's role is broader than the receptor construct. The remission data in B-cell malignancies are convincing, but the solid-tumour limits, toxicity and secondary-malignancy signals are still evolving. I would keep it as an alternative and not the lead.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks optogenetics (B026) second, as a widely adopted method that gave causal, cell-type-specific control, while acknowledging it is a method more than a disease mechanism and that choosing three of six names is a hard cut.
responses.response: Optogenetics has had a profound impact on research, and I do not dispute that. I am not persuaded that it should displace B003 or B040 this year. The six-person credit list means any trio would omit people with an equal claim (Bamberg, Boyden, Miesenböck), and the therapeutic extension is early. I would be open to revisiting it in a future year if the committee wants to recognise a tool, but that question is separate from this one.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide can be credited alongside Holst and Drucker without unfair omission of Habener or of Knudsen's drug-development role.
Whether the committee prefers a basic-physiology citation or one that explicitly covers the development of the therapies.
How strongly the Eshhar and Rosenberg attribution problems weigh against B040, and whether B003 or B040 is the better second choice if B034 stalls.
The supplied evidence does not allow me to settle priority disputes in the GLP-1 literature independently.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. My recorded co-authors (Vijay Kuchroo, Sven-Erik Sonesson) and my Bergen affiliation do not connect to any credited name on the shortlist. I work in autoimmunity, which is adjacent to B029 and B040, but that is a field overlap and not a personal tie.
